opportunities.title: Registration token subject can drift from returned user id
opportunities.summary: Parent bounty: #743 This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information. Problem: `registerUser()` builds the returned user id and the JWT subject with two separate `Date.now()` calls. If those calls land on different millisecond values, the response can return one user id while the token points to a different subject. Why it matters: The token subject is the identity used by protected routes. It should match the user id returned at registration. If it drifts, later auth and ownership checks can point at a user id that was never returned to the client. Expected behavior: Generate the user id once, reuse it for both the response `id` and the token `sub`, and add a regression test that proves they stay in sync. Scope: This is only about registration token subject consistency. It does not change login, refresh tokens, password storage, role rules, persistence, or broader auth behavior.

opportunities.title: Bug: Refresh endpoint mints tokens without validating a refresh token
opportunities.summary: ### Bug Description `POST /api/auth/refresh` currently ignores the request body and calls `refreshToken()` without validating any supplied refresh token. The service then returns a new access token for the hard-coded `usr_existing` user, so an unauthenticated caller can mint a fresh client token without presenting any credential. ### Expected Behavior The refresh endpoint should require a token in the request body, reject missing or invalid tokens, and only issue a replacement access token for the subject and role contained in a valid token. ### Reproduction 1. Start the API. 2. Send `POST /api/auth/refresh` with `{}` or no token. 3. Observe that the current code path mints a successful token instead of returning a 400/401 response. ### Proposed Fix - Add a refresh request schema requiring `token`. - Verify the supplied token before refreshing. - Preserve the decoded `sub` and `role` when issuing the replacement access token. - Add regression tests for missing, invalid, and valid token refresh requests. opportunities.title: [Bug bounty follow-up] tarsnap-recrypt can commit old-machine deletes while retaining a stale chunk directory
opportunities.summary: # [Bug bounty follow-up] tarsnap-recrypt can commit old-machine deletes while retaining a stale chunk directory I found a reproducible non-security crash-consistency gap in current `master` commit `0bf0b299fed91139044c81cc6fcdc5521c34d235` (`1.0.41-head`), after the fix for #746 / PR #747. At the end of `tarsnap-recrypt`, the old-machine delete transaction can be committed without any post-delete chunk directory being staged. An interruption or `unlink` failure immediately after that commit leaves a current sequence number but an old local directory which still claims that the deleted chunks exist. Disclosure: this issue was prepared with OpenAI Codex, an LLM, working on behalf of Sebastian Albrecht. The source path, commit state, subsequent deduplication decision, and fix control were independently rerun locally. Sebastian is available to discuss the report and answer technical questions. ## Cause The success tail in `recrypt/recrypt.c` performs: ```c storage_delete_end(SD); multitape_commit(ocachedir, omachinenum, oseqnum, 1, &storage_modified); unlink(odirpath); ``` Unlike a normal chunk deletion, this path never calls `chunks_delete_end` or `chunks_directory_write(..., ".tmp")`

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
